title: Tenant residency deprecation comms + risk checklist
content:
Purpose

Quick working draft: operator checklist + customer comm templates + risk register for planned deprecation of legacy tenant region pins (soft-pin v1). This doc is a single-file scratchpad intended for the migration working group (eng + solutions + legal + trust). Use it to capture decisions and to copy-paste comms.

Summary of intent

- Goal: migrate tenants from legacy soft-pin implementation to region-anchoring v2 (explicit pin + audit evidence) with minimal customer impact and clear audit trail. This is NOT a full engineering spec — those live in the route-routing repo PR referenced above.
- Scope: customers currently using /region?pin=soft or tenant metadata pins created before 2023-10-01. Excludes tenants already on dedicated or private-with-locality.
- Timeline (tentative): 2025-Feb to 2025-Apr (pilot -> staggered waves -> opt-out window -> enforcement).

Operator checklist (pre-rollout)

- [ ] Generate authoritative tenant export (tenant-id, created_at, pin_type, last_active_region). Script: tools/exports/tenant_pin_export_v1.sh — run in staging, then in prod with 48h window.
- [ ] Tag tenants with unknown/ambiguous metadata: add label pin:unknown for manual review.
- [ ] Build telemetry dashboard: pin-mismatch-rate, fallback-rate, error-504-by-region. Owner: Priya.
- [ ] Create canary cohort: 50 low-traffic tenants in EU/US/APAC across different org sizes.
- [ ] Confirm fallback policy mapping (v1->v2): see mapping table in linked PR.
- [ ] Prepare fallback artifact bundles: instructions for rollback (retain old routing SQL and rollback flag).
- [ ] Legal review: confirm customer contract language for region change acceptance. Link: CONFLUENCE:RD-REGION-POLICY-2024.
- [ ] Support playbook: pre-populated reply templates + escalation tags. Owner: Jordan.
- [ ] Run synthetic traffic tests: region pin drift simulation (script: tests/region_drift_sim.py).
- [ ] Ensure logs contain proof artifacts for audits (timestamped pin-change events, operator id, evidence bundle ID).

Risk register (concise)

- Risk: silent tenant breakage when anchor region changes. Mitigation: staged waves + monitoring of 5min error spikes + automated rollback for >3x baseline error-rate within 30 mins.
- Risk: legal/regulatory objection for regulated tenant. Mitigation: pre-check contracts + run opt-in for flagged customers; escalate to account lead.
- Risk: telemetry gaps (no signal to detect misrouting). Mitigation: instrumentation task with explicit telemetry fields (old_pin, new_pin, route_decision_reason).
- Risk: operator misconfiguration during rollouts. Mitigation: single-step rollout tooling with approval gate + audit trail; require two approvers for region changes on enterprise tenants.

Test cases to validate (operator + QA)

- TC-001: Tenant with soft-pin EU -> on-v2 pin remains EU, no routing change. (expected: 0% error increase)
- TC-002: Tenant with soft-pin ambiguous -> assign v2 anchor based on residency_preference; operator notice sent. (expected: manual review)
- TC-003: Model-serving failover to fallback region under v2 routing -> ensure data-handshake redaction and evidence stored.
- TC-004: Subpoena simulation: verify we can show a pinned-region-proof bundle for a random range of requests.
- TC-005: Performance check: median p95 latency across region transition is within SLO for canary cohort.

Customer communication templates (pick & edit)

- Short internal Slack note to account team (copy for quick send):

  Hey @account-ops, heads-up: we plan to migrate soft-region pins for tenant {{tenant_name}} on 2025-02-18 to v2 anchoring. No expected downtime; we will send customer notice 7 days prior. If this tenant has compliance constraints, flag immediately. Owner: @Jordan Lee.

- Customer email (technical audience)

  Subject: Upcoming change to regional pinning for your Redwood tenant

  Hi {{customer_contact}},

  We're planning a backend migration of legacy region pin metadata to our new region-anchoring system between 2025-02-18 and 2025-03-05. This change improves auditability and resilience (explicit pin proofs, per-route evidence bundles).

  Impact: None expected for typical workloads. If your org requires data residency guarantees tied to a specific jurisdiction, please reply to this email within 7 days and we'll schedule a brief alignment call.

  If you use custom routing or a self-managed network proxy, please let us know so we can coordinate.

  Thanks,
  Redwood Private Onboarding Team

- Customer email (legal/compliance audience)

  Subject: Notice: region pin metadata migration and auditability improvements

  Hi {{legal_contact}},

  As part of our ongoing improvements to regional compliance controls, we'll be consolidating legacy region pin metadata into a new auditable anchor system. This will not alter the physical region where your data is hosted — it formalizes our evidence collection and operator approval process for region changes.

  Reply within 7 days to request an exemption or to escalate to a contract review.

  Regards,
  Redwood Compliance Team

Rollback & emergency procedures

- Automated rollback trigger: if canary error-rate > 3x baseline AND latency p95 worsens by > 30% for 30m. Action: flip feature-flag region_pin_migration -> false, revert route-mapping table to snapshot, and notify SRE + product lead.
- Manual rollback: operator-run script rollback_pin_migration.sh --snapshot-id {{id}}. Requires two approvers.
- Post-rollback postmortem: 72h post incident, include timeline, metrics, artifact IDs.

Open questions / decisions needed

- Do we allow customers to permanently opt-out of v2 anchors (and remain on legacy soft-pin)? Legal says: "we should avoid long-term dual support." Need trade-off analysis by 2025-01-30.
- Telemetry retention: how long to keep evidence bundles for audit (default 1 year vs 7 years for enterprise)? Cost modeling required.
- Should we expose a tenant-level API to preview the v2 anchor decision before migration? UX team wants to avoid extra surface area; engineering cost estimate needed.

Notes to self / quick links

- Quick staging run commands: 
  - node tools/migrate_pins.js --env=staging --limit=100
  - curl -XPOST https://staging-internal.redwood/api/debug/pin-simulate -d '{"tenant":"t123","region":"eu"}'
- Slack thread for rollout coordination: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CPIN12345/p1670000000000
- Synthetic test harness: tests/region_migration_harness/README.md

Immediate next steps (this doc owner: Eli)

- Schedule 30m migration kickoff with stakeholders (eng, legal, support) by 2025-01-24.
- Confirm opt-out policy decision with legal by 2025-01-30.
- Produce customer-facing FAQ for public KB by 2025-02-01.

If you copy/paste any comms from this doc into customer emails, please update the dates and add the tracking JIRA key.
